name: Hurricane Chris
notes: A Shreveport chant record run through the ColliPark pipeline, and the parameter that separates it from the rest of the lane is the clap. The research says "heavy hand-clap layering on the hook", so `velocityTiers.accent` runs 104–122 — higher than the archetype — and `layerClapOffsetMs` is [2, 6], which is what makes a stack of hands sound like a stack rather than one sample. The hook melody is a two-pitch chant, so `motifPitchCount` is [2, 3] and `timbreHint` is `chant_stab`; the siren/whistle sample that is the record's signature is a `perc` lane rather than a melodic part, because it is a stab, not a line. The crowd-response section is `countermelody` at `answer_lick` weight 4 with `registerOffset` +12. ⛔ **`confidence` is low, matching the research's medium-low.** What is sourced is the ColliPark association and the era; everything numeric is inferred, and the 72–82 half-time band is marked [LOW-CONF] — so `session.bpm` 144–164 is the least defensible line in this file. ⚠ **The fill is not the fill the research names.** It says 808 tom rolls, and the engine's fill generator writes a snare roll with no way to route it onto the 808 — so `snareRoll.gapProb` 0.55 keeps what does fire sparse and broken rather than pretending to be a snare stream this record does not play. ⚠ The harmony is "minor, one-chord"; the `i–VI` family at weight 2 is **INFERRED** and carries the lowest weight, and the chord part's variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` [4, 14] and the 29-semitone voicing register instead. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 894 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, melody density [2,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
